tasks.title: Build a JavaScript Course Status
tasks.description: Create a simple JavaScript program that represents a student's course status using the fundamental JavaScript concepts covered in this module.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that stores a student's name, course name, completed lessons, and total lessons. Calculate the course progress percentage and print a meaningful course status in the console.
objectives: Use JavaScript variables or an object to store related student and course information.
Calculate a percentage using arithmetic operators.
Use JavaScript to produce a meaningful course status.
Display the final result using console.log().
requirements: Store the student's name and course name.
Store completed lessons and total lessons.
Calculate the progress percentage.
Print the student's name, course name, progress percentage, and status.
Use const or let appropriately.
tasks.hint: Use an object to keep the student and course information together. Calculate progress with completedLessons / totalLessons * 100, then use console.log() to display the result.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The student object keeps the related course information together. The progress is calculated using completed lessons divided by total lessons. A conditional expression determines whether the course is completed or still in progress, and console.log() displays the result.

tasks.title: Build a Student Result Calculator
tasks.description: Build a small JavaScript result calculator using variables, primitive values, arithmetic operators, comparisons, logical operators, and explicit type conversion.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that calculates a student's result from three subject marks. The marks are initially provided as strings, so convert them explicitly to numbers. Calculate the total and average, determine whether the student passed all subjects, and print a complete result summary.
objectives: Convert string values into numbers explicitly.
Use arithmetic operators to calculate total and average.
Use comparison and logical operators to determine the result.
Use meaningful variables to represent the student's result.
requirements: Store the student's name.
Store three subject marks as string values.
Convert all marks using Number().
Calculate total marks and average marks.
A subject is passed when its mark is at least 40.
The student passes only when all three subjects are passed.
Print the student name, total, average, and Pass or Fail status.
tasks.hint: Start by converting each mark with Number(). Calculate total and average separately. Check each subject with >= 40 and combine the conditions using &&.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The marks start as strings, so Number() performs explicit type conversion. Arithmetic operators calculate the total and average. Each mark is compared with 40, and the && operator requires all three conditions to be true before the student is considered passed.

tasks.title: Build a Course Enrollment Summary
tasks.description: Build a JavaScript course enrollment summary that combines variables, objects, primitive values, arithmetic, comparisons, logical operators, and explicit type conversion.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that generates a course enrollment summary for a student. The student's age, completed lessons, and total lessons are provided as string values. Convert the numeric values explicitly, validate the data, calculate progress, and print an appropriate enrollment status. If the numeric data is invalid or the total lessons value is zero or negative, print 'Invalid course data' instead.
objectives: Combine the fundamental JavaScript concepts covered in this module.
Use an object to organize student and course information.
Perform explicit type conversion before calculations.
Validate numeric data using comparisons and logical operators.
Calculate course progress and generate a meaningful status.
requirements: Create an object containing student name, age, course name, completed lessons, and total lessons.
Store age, completed lessons, and total lessons as string values initially.
Convert those values explicitly using Number().
Reject the data when any converted numeric value is NaN.
Reject the data when total lessons is zero or negative.
Reject the data when completed lessons is negative or greater than total lessons.
For valid data, calculate the progress percentage.
Print the student name, course name, age, progress, and enrollment status.
tasks.hint: Convert the string values before validation. Number.isNaN() can help detect invalid numeric conversion. Use && and || to combine validation conditions. Only calculate progress after the data passes validation.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The enrollment object stores all related information. Numeric values are explicitly converted with Number(). The validation combines Number.isNaN(), comparison operators, and logical operators to reject invalid data before any percentage calculation occurs. Once valid, progress is calculated and a status is selected according to the progress value.

tasks.title: Build a Student Performance and Role Checker
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript program that evaluates a student's performance and identifies the user's role using conditional logic and a switch statement.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a learning platform. Store a student's score and role. First, use if, else if and else to print whether the student has Excellent, Pass or Practice status based on the score. Then use a switch statement to print a message for the role: admin, student or guest.
requirements: Store a numeric student score in a JavaScript variable.
Use if, else if and else to determine the performance status.
Use a switch statement to handle admin, student and guest roles.
Print both the performance status and role message using console.log().
Handle a role that is not recognized with a default case.
objectives: Apply conditional logic to make decisions.
Use switch statements for multiple known cases.
Produce meaningful console output from JavaScript conditions.
tasks.hint: Start with a score variable and check the highest condition first. For the role, use switch(role) with separate cases for admin, student and guest, and include a default case.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The score is evaluated with if, else if and else so only the matching performance level is selected. The role is then handled with switch, where each known role has its own case and break. The default case handles any role that is not recognized.

tasks.title: Build a Course Progress Report
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript course progress report using loops and reusable functions with parameters and return values.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a student course containing several lessons. Store the lesson names in an array and the number of completed lessons separately. Use a loop to print every lesson name. Then create a reusable function that accepts completed lessons and total lessons and returns the completion percentage. Finally, print a meaningful course progress report.
requirements: Store multiple lesson names in an array.
Use a loop to print every lesson name.
Create a reusable function with parameters.
Return the calculated completion percentage from the function.
Handle the case where the total number of lessons is zero.
Print the final progress percentage.
objectives: Use loops to repeat an operation over course lessons.
Create reusable functions with parameters.
Use return values to produce calculated results.
Combine loops and functions in a practical JavaScript program.
tasks.hint: Use for...of to iterate through the lesson array. Create a function such as calculateProgress(completed, total) and return 0 when total is zero to avoid an invalid calculation.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The lessons array stores the course lessons and for...of visits each lesson one by one. calculateProgress() receives completed and total as parameters and returns the percentage. The zero-total check prevents division by zero. The returned value is then printed as the course progress.

tasks.title: Build a Course Progress Tracker
tasks.description: Create a reusable course progress tracker using arrow functions, callbacks and a closure.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript course progress tracker that processes lesson scores and keeps track of how many lessons have been evaluated. Use an arrow function as a callback to transform the lesson scores into progress values. Then create a closure-based tracker function that remembers how many lessons have been processed between calls. Print the processed scores and the final number of processed lessons.
requirements: Store multiple lesson scores in an array.
Use an arrow function as a callback to process each score.
Use an array method that accepts a callback.
Create a closure that preserves a private counter between function calls.
Call the closure for every lesson that is processed.
Print the processed scores and processed lesson count.
objectives: Use arrow functions as callback functions.
Understand how callbacks are passed to array methods.
Create and use a closure with preserved lexical scope.
Combine callbacks and closures in a practical JavaScript program.
tasks.hint: Use map() with an arrow function to transform each score. For the closure, create a function that contains a private count variable and returns another function that increments and returns that count.
tasks.solutionExplanation: map() receives an arrow function callback and creates a new array from the lesson scores. createLessonTracker() contains processedCount inside its local scope and returns a function that can still access that variable after createLessonTracker() finishes. This preserved access is the closure. Each processed lesson calls trackLesson(), which increments the private counter.

tasks.title: Build a Student Course Profile
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript program that manages a student's enrolled courses and profile information using arrays and objects.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a learning platform. Store a student's name, progress percentage and enrolled courses. The enrolled courses must be stored in an array. Add one more course to the array, then create a student object containing the student's information and courses. Finally, print the student's name, progress and complete course list to the console.
requirements: Create an array containing at least three course names.
Add another course to the array.
Create an object representing the student.
Store the student's name, progress and courses in the object.
Access and print the student's information using object properties.
Print every enrolled course using the course array.
objectives: Create and manipulate arrays.
Create objects that represent real-world entities.
Access object properties and array values.
Combine arrays and objects in a practical JavaScript program.
tasks.hint: Start with a courses array and use push() to add another course. Then create a student object with name, progress and courses properties. Use console.log() to display the information.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The courses array stores the student's enrolled courses and push() adds another course. The student object groups the student's name, progress and courses into one real-world entity. The object properties are accessed with dot notation, and the courses array is traversed with for...of.

tasks.title: Build a Course Progress Analyzer
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript course progress analyzer using objects, array methods, destructuring, spread and safe access with default values.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that analyzes several course lessons. Each lesson must contain a title and completion status. Use array methods to find the completed lessons, create a list of lesson titles, and calculate whether all required lessons are completed. Then create a new student profile from an existing object using spread syntax and safely read an optional profile city using optional chaining and nullish coalescing. Print the analysis results to the console.
requirements: Store lesson data as an array of objects.
Use filter() to find completed lessons.
Use map() to create a list containing lesson titles.
Use every() to determine whether all lessons are completed.
Use destructuring to extract a property from an object.
Use spread syntax to create an updated object without modifying the original object.
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing to safely read a missing nested value.
Print all analysis results to the console.
objectives: Work with arrays containing objects.
Apply map(), filter() and every() to practical data.
Use destructuring for clean property access.
Use spread syntax for object transformation.
Safely handle optional nested data.
tasks.hint: Represent each lesson as an object such as { title, completed }. filter() can select completed lessons, map() can extract titles and every() can check whether every lesson is completed. Use const { name } = student to destructure and {...student, progress: newValue} to create an updated object.
tasks.solutionExplanation: filter() creates an array containing only completed lessons, while map() creates a new array containing lesson titles. every() returns true only when every lesson satisfies the completion condition. Destructuring extracts name from the student object. Spread creates updatedStudent as a new object while preserving the original values. Optional chaining safely checks address.city, and ?? supplies Unknown when the value is null or undefined.

tasks.title: Build a Unique Student Score Registry
tasks.description: Build a practical student score registry that combines arrays, objects, array methods, destructuring, spread, optional data, Map and Set.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a learning platform that manages student scores. Several score records may contain the same student ID. Use a Set to identify the unique student IDs and a Map to store each student's latest score. Use array methods to create a list of passing students and calculate the average score. Create an updated student record using destructuring and spread syntax. Also safely read an optional student location with optional chaining and nullish coalescing. Print the registry summary and final results to the console.
requirements: Store multiple score records as objects containing studentId, name and score.
Use Set to create a collection of unique student IDs.
Use Map to associate each student ID with its latest score.
Use filter() to identify students whose score is at least 60.
Use reduce() to calculate the average score.
Use destructuring to extract student information.
Use spread syntax to create an updated student record.
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing for optional location data.
Print the unique student count, score registry, passing students and average score.
objectives: Use Map and Set for specialized collections.
Combine objects with advanced array methods.
Transform and summarize structured data.
Use destructuring and spread for object transformations.
Safely handle missing nested information.
tasks.hint: Create a Set from the student IDs to remove duplicates. Use a Map and set() for each score record so repeated IDs update the stored score. filter() can find passing records and reduce() can calculate the total score. Destructure the selected student's fields and use spread to create an updated record.
tasks.solutionExplanation: Set removes duplicate student IDs because each value can appear only once. Map stores a student ID with its latest score, so the later s1 record replaces the earlier score. filter() selects passing records and reduce() calculates the total used for the average. Destructuring extracts selectedStudent properties, while spread creates updatedStudent without changing the original object. Optional chaining safely accesses profile.city and ?? provides Unknown when the city is unavailable.

tasks.title: Build an Interactive Course Status Card
tasks.description: Create a small browser-based course status card using DOM element selection, content updates and class manipulation.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a simple HTML page containing a course status card. The page must have a heading with id 'title', a paragraph with id 'status', and a button with id 'completeBtn'. Using JavaScript, select these elements and make the button update the status text to 'Course Completed' when clicked. Also add the 'active' class to the course heading after the button is clicked.
requirements: Create or use an element with id 'title'.
Create or use an element with id 'status'.
Create or use a button with id 'completeBtn'.
Select the required elements using querySelector().
Update the status element's text using textContent.
Add a CSS class to the heading using classList.add().
Make the interaction happen when the button is clicked.
objectives: Understand how JavaScript interacts with the DOM.
Select DOM elements using querySelector().
Change element content with textContent.
Change an element's classes using classList.
tasks.hint: Give the elements predictable IDs so they can be selected with document.querySelector(). Add a click listener to the button, then update status.textContent and use title.classList.add('active').
tasks.solutionExplanation: querySelector() finds the required DOM elements. addEventListener() waits for the button's click event. When the button is clicked, textContent changes the status message and classList.add() adds the active class to the heading.

tasks.title: Build a Student Enrollment Form Validator
tasks.description: Create a browser-based student enrollment form that reads submitted values, validates the input and displays useful feedback without reloading the page.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a student enrollment form containing a student name input, email input and a submit button. Using JavaScript, listen for the form's submit event and prevent the browser's default page reload. Read the entered values, validate that the name is not empty and that the email contains '@'. If the data is invalid, display an error message in the page. If the data is valid, display a success message containing the student's name.
requirements: Create or use a form with id 'enrollmentForm'.
Create or use a name input with id 'studentName'.
Create or use an email input with id 'studentEmail'.
Create or use an element with id 'message' for validation feedback.
Listen for the form submit event.
Call preventDefault() so the page does not reload.
Read the submitted form values.
Validate that the name is not empty.
Validate that the email contains '@'.
Display either an error or success message in the DOM.
objectives: Handle form submit events.
Read user-entered form values.
Prevent the browser's default form submission.
Apply basic client-side validation.
Display validation results dynamically.
tasks.hint: Use form.addEventListener('submit', event => {}). Call event.preventDefault() first. Read input.value, validate the values, and update message.textContent depending on whether the data is valid.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The submit event is handled with addEventListener(). preventDefault() stops the browser from performing its normal form submission. The input values are read with value and trim() removes unnecessary whitespace. The conditions validate the required fields. Depending on the result, textContent updates the message displayed on the page.

tasks.title: Build a Persistent Course Progress Tracker
tasks.description: Build an interactive course progress tracker that combines DOM manipulation, events, form validation and localStorage.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a browser-based course progress tracker. The page must contain a form where a student can enter a course name and completed lesson count, a status area and a button or submit action to save the progress. Validate that the course name is present and the completed lesson count is a valid non-negative number. Display the saved progress in the page and store it in localStorage so that the progress is restored automatically when the page is opened again. The student must be able to update the saved progress by submitting the form again.
requirements: Create or use a form with id 'progressForm'.
Create or use a course name input with id 'courseName'.
Create or use a completed lessons input with id 'completedLessons'.
Create or use an element with id 'progressStatus'.
Handle the form submit event.
Prevent the default form submission.
Validate that the course name is not empty.
Validate that completed lessons is a valid non-negative number.
Store the progress data in localStorage using JSON.stringify().
Read saved progress from localStorage using JSON.parse().
Restore the saved progress when the page loads.
Update the DOM whenever progress is saved or restored.
objectives: Combine DOM selection and manipulation.
Handle form events and user input.
Validate browser form data.
Persist structured data with localStorage.
Use JSON.stringify() and JSON.parse() for stored data.
Build a small interactive browser feature using multiple DOM concepts together.
tasks.hint: Create one object containing courseName and completedLessons. Save it with localStorage.setItem('courseProgress', JSON.stringify(data)). On page load, use localStorage.getItem() and JSON.parse() to restore it. Check for null before trying to use the saved value.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The form submit event is intercepted with preventDefault(). The entered values are validated before a progress object is created. JSON.stringify() converts the object into a string that localStorage can store. On page load, getItem() retrieves the saved string and JSON.parse() converts it back into an object. renderProgress() keeps the DOM update reusable for both saving and restoring progress.

tasks.title: Build a Localized Student Welcome Card
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript program that generates a personalized student course welcome message and formats the enrollment date for an Indian locale.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a learning platform. Store a student's name, course name, progress percentage, and enrollment date. Use a template literal to generate a complete welcome message containing the student's name, course name, and progress. Then use Intl.DateTimeFormat with the en-IN locale to display the enrollment date in a readable format. Print the final welcome information to the console.
requirements: Store the student information using JavaScript variables or an object.
Use a template literal to create the personalized welcome message.
Use Intl.DateTimeFormat with the en-IN locale to format the enrollment date.
Print the formatted information to the console.
objectives: Use template literals to create readable dynamic strings.
Format a JavaScript Date using Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Combine multiple pieces of data into a meaningful output.
Produce a clean console-based student welcome card.
tasks.hint: Use backticks with ${} for the dynamic message and Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-IN', { dateStyle: 'medium' }) to format the date.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The student object stores the required course information. The template literal inserts the student's name, course and progress directly into a readable message. Intl.DateTimeFormat formats the enrollment date according to the Indian locale. Finally, both pieces of information are printed to the console.

tasks.title: Build a Modular Student Profile Utility
tasks.description: Create a small modular JavaScript utility that validates a student's email and generates a formatted course profile.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript application using ES Modules. Create a student data module that exports a student object containing name, email, course, progress, and enrollment date. Create a separate profile utility module that imports the student data, validates the email using a regular expression, formats the enrollment date using Intl.DateTimeFormat with the en-IN locale, and returns a readable student profile using a template literal. Import the profile utility into the main JavaScript file and print the generated profile to the console.
requirements: Create and export student data from a separate JavaScript module.
Import the student data into another module.
Validate the student's email using a regular expression.
Format the enrollment date using Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Generate the final profile using a template literal.
Import and execute the profile utility from the main file.
objectives: Understand how ES Modules separate application responsibilities.
Use regular expressions for controlled email validation.
Use Intl.DateTimeFormat for localized dates.
Combine imported data with reusable JavaScript functions.
Create a readable modular student profile.
tasks.hint: Use export/import between files. A simple email pattern such as /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ can be tested with .test().
tasks.solutionExplanation: The student data is kept in student.js and exported so other modules can use it. profile.js imports no student-specific values directly; instead it exposes a reusable createStudentProfile function. The regular expression checks whether the email has a basic valid structure. Intl.DateTimeFormat converts the Date into an en-IN formatted date. The template literal builds the complete profile. main.js imports both the student data and reusable function, then prints the result.

tasks.title: Build a Course ID Generator and Validator
tasks.description: Build a modular JavaScript course ID system that generates sequential course IDs, validates them with regular expressions, and produces a localized enrollment report.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a modular JavaScript course enrollment utility. Build a generator function that produces sequential course IDs in the format JS-2026-001, JS-2026-002 and so on. Export the generator from one module and import it into the main module. Generate three course IDs and validate each generated ID using a regular expression. Store the generated enrollment records with student names and enrollment dates. Use template literals to create a readable enrollment report and Intl.DateTimeFormat with the en-IN locale to format each enrollment date. Print the complete report to the console.
requirements: Create a generator function using function* and yield.
Generate sequential course IDs in the JS-YYYY-NNN format.
Export the generator from a JavaScript module.
Import and use the generator from the main module.
Validate generated IDs using a regular expression.
Use template literals to create the enrollment report.
Format enrollment dates using Intl.DateTimeFormat with en-IN.
Print all generated enrollment records to the console.
objectives: Use generators and iterators to produce sequential values.
Use ES Modules to organize reusable functionality.
Use regular expressions for structured ID validation.
Combine generated data with objects and localized dates.
Build a complete reusable course enrollment utility.
tasks.hint: Use function* with yield for sequential IDs. A pattern such as /^JS-\d{4}-\d{3}$/ validates the required ID format. Use Intl.DateTimeFormat for the enrollment date.
tasks.solutionExplanation: courseIdGenerator.js exports a generator function. Each call to next() resumes the generator and produces the next sequential ID using yield. String.padStart ensures the numeric portion always contains three digits. The regular expression checks that every generated ID follows the JS-YYYY-NNN structure. The main module stores students as objects, combines each student with a generated ID, validates the ID, formats the enrollment date using Intl.DateTimeFormat, and uses a template literal to print a readable enrollment report.

tasks.title: Build an Asynchronous Course Loader
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript program that loads course information asynchronously and displays the result after the asynchronous operation completes.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that simulates loading a course from a server. Create a function that returns a Promise and resolves with the message 'JavaScript Course Loaded' after a short delay. Create an async function that waits for the Promise using await and then prints the returned message to the console. Also print 'Loading course...' before waiting so that the asynchronous execution order can be observed.
requirements: Create a Promise that represents an asynchronous course-loading operation.
Resolve the Promise after a short delay using setTimeout.
Create an async function to handle the course loading.
Use await to wait for the Promise result.
Print a loading message before the asynchronous operation.
Print the resolved course message after the operation completes.
objectives: Understand the difference between synchronous and asynchronous execution.
Create and consume a Promise.
Use async and await for readable asynchronous code.
Observe the order in which asynchronous operations execute.
tasks.hint: Create a new Promise and use setTimeout inside it. Resolve the Promise with the course message, then await it inside an async function.
tasks.solutionExplanation: loadCourse returns a Promise representing an asynchronous operation. setTimeout delays the operation and resolve() changes the Promise to the fulfilled state with the course message. startCourse is declared async so it can use await. The loading message is printed immediately, while await pauses the async function until the Promise is fulfilled. The final course message is then printed.

tasks.title: Build a Course Dashboard Data Loader
tasks.description: Create an asynchronous course dashboard loader that fetches independent course and lesson data concurrently and handles HTTP failures.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript function that loads course information and lesson information for a learning dashboard. The course and lesson endpoints are independent, so load both resources concurrently using Promise.all. Use fetch with async and await. Before using the returned data, check the response ok property and throw an Error when an HTTP request fails. Handle the error with try/catch and print either the loaded course dashboard data or a meaningful error message.
requirements: Create a function for loading course and lesson data.
Use fetch to request both resources.
Check response.ok for each request before using the response data.
Convert successful responses to JSON.
Use Promise.all to load the independent resources concurrently.
Use async and await.
Handle failures using try/catch.
Print a meaningful success or error message.
objectives: Use the Fetch API to request JSON data.
Understand HTTP failure handling with response.ok.
Use async and await with multiple asynchronous operations.
Use Promise.all for concurrent independent requests.
Handle asynchronous errors safely.
tasks.hint: Create two fetch promises and pass them to Promise.all. After each response is received, check response.ok before calling response.json(). Wrap the whole operation in try/catch.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The function starts both fetch requests without waiting for either one to finish, then Promise.all waits for both responses. response.ok is checked because fetch does not automatically reject for HTTP errors such as 404 or 500. If a response is unsuccessful, an Error is thrown and execution moves to catch. After both responses are successful, their JSON bodies are read concurrently with another Promise.all. The final result is printed, while any asynchronous failure is handled by the catch block.

tasks.title: Build a Cancellable Course Dashboard Loader
tasks.description: Build a robust asynchronous course dashboard loader that loads independent resources concurrently and allows the operation to be cancelled safely.
tasks.problemStatement: Build a JavaScript course dashboard loader that requests course data and lesson data concurrently. Both requests must use the same AbortController signal. Use Promise.all with async and await to coordinate the independent requests. Validate both HTTP responses before reading their JSON data. The dashboard loader must expose a way to cancel the pending requests using AbortController.abort(). Handle normal HTTP failures separately from cancellation so that cancellation produces a clear 'Course loading cancelled' message instead of a generic error. When loading succeeds, print the course and lesson data.
requirements: Create an AbortController for the dashboard loading operation.
Pass the controller signal to both fetch requests.
Load the independent course and lesson requests concurrently.
Use Promise.all with async and await.
Check response.ok for both HTTP responses.
Read successful responses as JSON.
Provide a cancellation function that calls controller.abort().
Handle AbortError separately from other errors.
Print a clear success, cancellation, or failure message.
objectives: Combine Fetch API, Promises and async/await in a realistic workflow.
Use Promise.all for concurrent asynchronous operations.
Cancel pending fetch operations using AbortController.
Distinguish cancellation from normal asynchronous failures.
Build safer asynchronous application logic with cleanup support.
tasks.hint: Create one AbortController and pass controller.signal to every fetch. Calling controller.abort() cancels requests using that signal. In catch, check error.name === 'AbortError' before handling other errors.
tasks.solutionExplanation: createCourseDashboardLoader creates one AbortController for the complete dashboard operation. Both fetch requests receive the same signal, so aborting the controller can cancel both requests. Promise.all allows the independent requests to run concurrently. Each response is checked with response.ok before its JSON body is read. The returned cancel function calls controller.abort(). If cancellation happens, fetch rejects with an AbortError, which is handled separately so the user receives a clear cancellation message. Other errors are handled as normal dashboard failures.
